title: Carter's repertoire and the saxophone writing on Sleep
summary: Standards, Carter's arrangements, and his saxophone sheets of sound, which Johnson says predated Coltrane's.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Back to the Benny Carter years, what was the repertoire that you were playing with Benny Carter?
Benny’s repertoire included standards and his very unique personal arrangements of standards and some of his own works, shall we call them. I don’t recall the names of them.
Was this still pretty much playing for dances?
Not just playing for dances, but mostly. I wish I could think of some of the tunes we played, other than Sleep.
Yeah, I remember that one. Yeah.

Sleep is the one that had the complex saxophone section with a thousand notes. You know, it’s a funny thing. They associate [John] Coltrane with this term "sheets of sound." Little do they know. Benny Carter [laughs] was the originator of "sheets of sound" for saxophone sections, not just one guy.
